purpose: Prevent vehicle-quality improvements from being accounted only as surviving tanks. Every extra vehicle sortie/tank-day must propagate through the combined-arms system and its costs.
core_unit: combat-effective vehicle-day (tank-day / AFV-day), not only end-state hull survival

own_force_benefit: infantry casualties avoided because tanks suppress/absorb enemy fire
trucks/prime movers/engineer assets preserved during movement or withdrawal
wounded and disabled equipment recovered under armored cover
enemy salvage denied when battlefield possession changes
enemy_cost: AT guns/artillery/MG positions destroyed or suppressed
extra ammunition/fuel/repair burden caused by repeated Japanese contacts
own_force_cost: additional exposure and hence additional damaged vehicles/crew casualties

annihilated_force_rule.principle: If a garrison/formation is ultimately annihilated or captured, its final residual hull/personnel value may still be zero, but earlier survival is not erased.
persisting_effects: additional enemy casualties inflicted before destruction
friendly infantry/artillery surviving longer before final collapse
evacuation/recovery opportunities created for other formations
annihilated_force_rule.guard: Do not convert temporary survival into national surviving strength if no withdrawal/recovery route exists.

combined_arms_cap.rule: Vehicle improvements are capped by the weakest binding system: fuel, bridges/roads, infantry/engineer/artillery coordination, ammunition, communications, air attack, battlefield possession.
combined_arms_cap.effect: A reliable tank that cannot be fueled, bridged, supported or recovered does not create proportional combat power.
